variants.name: A1 — Udaipur as a day trip
variants.how: Third night in Chittorgarh. Day 4 runs Chittorgarh → Udaipur (07:00, arrive 09:15) → City Palace, Pichola, lunch at Viraasat → depart 16:30 → back in Chittorgarh 18:45. Day 5 becomes Chittorgarh → Mount Abu, 285 km via Nathdwara.
variants.tradeoff: +240 km on Day 4 and a 285 km Day 5. Saves a night's accommodation, gains a third Chittorgarh evening.

variants.name: A2 — Udaipur as a pass-through ★ recommended fallback
variants.how: Day 4 runs Chittorgarh 07:00 → Udaipur 09:15 → City Palace + lunch + Pichola until 15:00 → Mount Abu by 19:00. The freed night goes to Jaisalmer as a third night, or to Barmer to split the long haul.
variants.tradeoff: No Sajjangarh sunset, no Udaipur evening. But it converts a costly night into an extra Jaisalmer day — which fits your priorities better than anything else here.

variants.name: B — Split the long haul
variants.how: Add a Barmer night. Day 6 becomes Mount Abu → Barmer (260 km, arrive mid-afternoon — ajrak block-printing workshops and the Kiradu temple ruins 35 km out, an 11th-century complex almost nobody visits). Day 7 becomes Barmer → Jaisalmer (155 km) arriving 11:00.
variants.tradeoff: Costs one extra day overall. Removes the hardest driving day entirely.

variants.name: C — Jodhpur instead of Mount Abu
variants.how: Udaipur → Ranakpur (1,444 carved marble pillars, no two alike) → Jodhpur (Mehrangarh, the best-preserved fort in Rajasthan, and the blue city) → Jaisalmer. Legs become 165, 165 and 285 km.
variants.tradeoff: No 480 km day anywhere, and the non-veg situation improves a lot — Jodhpur is a serious meat-eating city. You lose Dilwara and the hill-station night. On sightseeing density and road quality this is objectively the better circuit; it's only wrong if Mount Abu specifically matters to you.

items: No night driving outside cities. Unlit tractor trolleys, camel carts, livestock and trucks with dead tail lights are all normal. Every arrival in this plan is timed before sunset for that reason.
Rural speed discipline: 60–70 km/h on two-lane roads, not 90. Free-roaming cattle everywhere; blackbuck and chinkara in the west.
Riskiest overtaking is on the Pushkar–Bhilwara and Sanchore–Barmer stretches. Wait for real visibility.
Ghats: Nag Pahar, the Abu ghat, Sajjangarh's approach. Engine-brake down; don't ride the friction brakes.
FASTag with a healthy balance. Most of the toll is on the two Delhi legs.
Jaipur: Jaleb Chowk or Ramniwas Bagh. You're only there two hours.
Ajmer: Ana Sagar side. Don't take the car toward the Dargah.
Pushkar: main lot at the town edge; everything is walk-only.
Chittorgarh: the happy exception — drive the entire internal fort circuit.
Udaipur: the weakest point of the trip. Gangaur Ghat paid lot, ~₹30/hr.
Jaisalmer: Gopa Chowk below the fort. Never drive into the fort lanes.
Sam Dunes: park on the road; the sand is for the jeeps.
Tyre pressures cold including the spare, +2–3 psi rear for the extra passenger and luggage.
Coolant, oil, washer reservoir topped — refill washer fluid twice on the trip. Desert dust on the windscreen at sunset is genuinely dangerous.
Roadside assistance number saved offline. Signal is patchy between Sanchore and Barmer.
The Victoris's 210 mm ground clearance is ample for everything here, including the Dhorimanna section and the Sam approach road.
Boot space is 439 L. Three people's luggage fits — pack soft bags, not hard cases, and keep the rear view clear.
October–March is the window. Days 22–28°C; desert nights near freezing in Dec–Jan.
April–June makes Day 6 punishing — western Rajasthan passes 45°C and AC load costs 2–3 kmpl.
July–September is green in the south and Menal Falls actually flows, but the Abu ghat gets slow in heavy rain.
Avoid Pushkar Camel Fair week (usually November) unless you're going for it — Ajmer and Pushkar rates triple.

sources: Vehicle — Maruti Suzuki Victoris specs via CarWale, CarDekho, ZigWheels, 91Wheels: 45 L tank; ARAI 21.18 kmpl (petrol MT), 21.06 (petrol AT), 28.65 (strong hybrid), 27.02 km/kg (CNG). CarWale real-world testing returned 20.24 kmpl highway on the hybrid.
Fuel prices — New Delhi ₹102.12/L and Jaipur ₹113.35/L, published 12–14 Sep 2026. Rajasthan carries the highest state VAT on petrol in India.

Distances — Google Maps road figures per leg. The Mount Abu–Jaisalmer leg was cross-checked against independent traveller accounts reporting 430–500 km and 8–9 h via Sanchore and Barmer, with ~40 km of poor surface.
